### 1.1 Version rule
* Current documents MUST say integer `schema_version: 4`. No silent migration. `2`, `3`, future versions and absent versions fail `schema_version_unsupported` before any write/provisioning/trigger registration. * Historical v2 validation may remain a separately invoked compatibility command using `../../contracts/historical-v2/config.schema.json`; it MUST NOT arm a v4 deployment. The assertion in VOLD-001 that a const-2 document is an unchanged valid const-4 document is superseded for this candidate: **data can be migrated, bytes cannot be identical while changing the version**. * Migration is explicit operator work: emit an old/new field diff; move agent `model/context_limit/max_turns/token_budget` into `runtime.model/context_window/max_turns/token_budget`; require an explicit provider; map singular `approval` to `approvals`; replace `capability` or legacy `grants/grantable_pool` with all three `permissions` scopes and separate `create_subordinate`; map `sessions` or per-agent `session.fork_policy` into root `session`; add all missing required blocks. Both spellings together are a migration conflict, never last-writer-wins. New identity/profile references require actual provisioning/readback, not a rename-only migration. * `registry[].mirror_key` gains the required leading slash. All existing sessions retain their snapshots; migration cannot rewrite their authority or protected state. A submitted v4 file containing any legacy key fails `unknown_field`.

### 1.2 Deliberate format decisions (not historical owner-confirmed defaults)
This deliverable chooses concrete mechanics where the source only names a requirement. These are design outputs for integration, not claims of prior owner approval:
1. Every top-level block is present, including disabled subsystems. Explicit empty lists are legal where shown. Every field without a source-backed default is **required**, except `workers[].temporary_config` (conditional). No guessed model, provider, security policy, retention, numeric cap or lifetime default is introduced. 2. Gateway `max_inflight` is required. The source's **4 main / 2 remote** are deployment examples, not a universal rule deducible from a gateway ID. `orchestration.stale_after_s` is required because “2× cycle” is ambiguous for multiple cron clocks. The full example selects 7200 explicitly, not as a loader default. Admission owner/fallback are also required-explicit: VOL-C §6.7 proposes controller-local/true, but §11.7 marks that proposal not user-confirmed; the example deliberately chooses controller-local/false. 3. `ingress.bind/public_url/credential_ref`, `scheduler.*`, `capacity.per_role`, `projects[]`, `identity`, `allowed_workdirs`, and `temporary_config` are the exact homes for previously untyped requirements. No extra `config`, `settings`, or untyped extension bag is permitted. 4. Static managed foremen/workers reside in `workers[]`; director/manager/supervisor rows reside in `agents[]`. IDs and identities are unique across both arrays. Runtime worker creation uses the same explicit shape, with its work-specific values carried in the operation rather than silently writing the VP file. 5. `create_subordinate` includes `foreman|worker` as well as `none|supervisor|manager`, reconciling the newer explicit-worker path with VOLD-010's obsolete restriction. Values name the maximum tier permitted, as defined in §5; the field alone is not provisioned credentials. 6. Permission classes keep the canonical names `use`, `grant`, `confer_delegation`; `create_subordinate` remains independent. Root static grants have no runtime lineage fields. Issued GrantRecords, expiry, revocation and `authority_ref` live in the durable control store, not in this file. 7. Root `session` is the only fork-policy location. VP-authored project overrides precede agent overrides, then global. The two modes are **not** ordered by strictness. See §5.3; this replaces G-09's undefined “narrower mode” test. 8. The candidate makes `runtime.max_turns` and `runtime.token_budget` required along with provider/model/context, satisfying RL-19 without an unconfirmed fallback limit. `approvals.gates` contains exact action identifiers, not the historical four-item enum that contradicted VOL-D's `payment`/`delete` examples. 9. Integer fields are bounded at 9007199254740991 unless a smaller maximum is listed, to keep JSON canonicalization exact across Go and JSON consumers. This is an encoding bound, not a tuned operational default. An overflowing derived value is an error; do not wrap or clamp it. All five roles are representable in explicit recipient selectors. The three project conflict policies are a closed enumeration, not executable text.

### 2. File syntax and load boundary
The logical document is a JSON-compatible object. Recommended file is `harness.yaml`; `.json` is equivalent. The original `harness.toml` name remains supported with TOML 1.0 decoding into the identical object.
* UTF-8, one document, string keys, case-sensitive exact names. Preserve `hermesBinding` camel case; all other spellings are shown in the registry. Do not accept guessed aliases. * Reject duplicate keys/tables, YAML aliases/anchors/merge keys, custom tags, malformed UTF-8, non-finite numbers, YAML timestamp objects and trailing documents. No shell expansion, environment interpolation, `~` expansion, includes or implicit overlay search. `${TOKEN}` is literal text, never a credential value. YAML booleans are only `true` and `false`. * JSON integers use integer syntax, not floats or booleans; ranges are as registered. YAML numbers use JSON decimal syntax (no octal, hex, sexagesimal or underscored integers); TOML uses its native numeric syntax with the same decoded type/range checks. Explicit YAML tags, including standard tags, are forbidden. `_s` is integer seconds; `_days` integer days; budgets/context are token counts; `_bytes` is bytes. A configured zero is accepted only where `minimum: 0` is registered; it never means unlimited. In Go, validate with `json.Number`/token-kind retention before decoding to `int64`; converting everything to `float64` loses the integer-token distinction. Check seconds-to-duration overflow before conversion, or use integer deadlines instead of a nanosecond duration for long horizons. * `null` is legal only for `storage.classes.*.{namespace,sync_owner,conflict_rule}`. JSON/YAML spell it explicitly. TOML has no null: omission of exactly those fields normalizes to null before structural validation; no other omission is translated to null. Active route rules can still reject null. * Closed objects reject unknown keys. The **only typed maps** are `storage.tool_class` (tool identifier → one of four class names) and `session.per_agent_override/per_project_override` (known ID → fork mode). Map values are validated, never free JSON; override map keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`. * Strings with `minLength: 1` cannot be blank/whitespace-only. References are opaque exact names unless their schema says path, URL, ID or pattern. Identifiers are never normalized. No inline secrets. File-token references are absolute paths; logical profile references begin `/chd/credentials/` and are resolved by the deployment's authenticated credential store. A missing credential is a readiness failure, not an invitation to use another profile's token. * URL origins contain scheme, hostname and optional port, no user-info/query/fragment/path/trailing slash. Hostname syntax and `http|https` match the schema; ports are 1–65535. This revision deliberately does not accept IPv6 literals (schema excludes brackets/colons in hosts). `transport: loopback` requires `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`; tunnels must terminate at an operator-provisioned endpoint; CHD does not create SSH tunnels from config text. Non-loopback plaintext is accepted only with a deployment-level verified private transport; readiness must reject an unprotected direct HTTP route. * Paths are absolute, cannot contain NUL or a `..` segment, and must resolve inside allowed roots after symlink resolution **on the target host**. `/srv/chd/work-evil` is not inside `/srv/chd/work`. Never check a remote workdir only on the controller and call it valid. * Cron strings are five fields, UTC: minute 0–59, hour 0–23, day 1–31, month 1–12, weekday 0–6. Allow `*`, lists, ascending ranges and positive step expressions within each field range; no seconds, names, `@every`, `?`, timezone prefix or weekday 7. Scheduler supplies calendar behavior (restricted day-of-month/day-of-week use OR). CHD registers ordinary scheduler triggers; it never runs a cron engine. `[]` means event-driven; a supervisor must have `[]`.

### 2.1 Ordered algorithm and errors
1. Parse with duplicate/type preservation; require version 4. 2. Validate raw structure with Draft 2020-12. `default` is an annotation, **not** automatic mutation. Required absence fails even if an implementation has a zero value. In Go, pointer/optional fields or raw-message presence tracking MUST distinguish absent, `false`, `0`, `[]`, `{}`, and null. 3. Copy input; insert only registered defaults and the derived wait timeout. Revalidate the effective object. Record default provenance and the source requirement. Do not mutate the submitted file. 4. Check unique identities/references, then policy/storage/limit consistency (§4–§5), then warnings. Use structured `{code,json_path,detail}` errors. Return nonzero / refuse activation on any error; never partially create agents or scheduler lanes for an invalid file. A warning cannot downgrade an error. 5. Validate external prerequisites: tool/capability/action catalog, skill assets and explicit specialization deltas, project paths, host/profile identity, credential access, current VP revision and authority, transport security, tool restriction enforcement, storage durability/fencing capability, scheduler trigger readback (scheduled readiness only), and archive-adapter compatibility. These are separate from structural validation and MUST be recorded as `not_checked|ready|failed`, not assumed green. 6. Stage a desired revision, converge profiles and read back each effective revision/digest. Publish ready only for verified targets. Preserve prior effective revision on failure. Register changed triggers through the scheduler's validated API, never by direct database edits. No runtime/secret/learned-state replacement is smuggled through this file.
Primary static errors: `schema_version_unsupported`, `parse_error`, `unknown_field`, `required_missing`, `schema_invalid`, `duplicate_id`, `unknown_gateway`, `profile_shared`, `principal_shared`, `policy_owner_mismatch`, `registry_mismatch`, `unknown_participant`, `room_membership_mismatch`, `bond_room_mismatch`, `bond_kind_mismatch`, `unknown_dispatch_target`, `unknown_agent`, `unknown_project`, `workspace_not_allowed`, `path_invalid`, `cron_invalid`, `tool_without_grant`, `tool_rule_conflict`, `use_not_delegable`, `supervisor_delegation_forbidden`, `control_route_invalid`, `archive_route_invalid`, `project_route_invalid`, `measurement_band_reversed`. Error messages must never include resolved token bytes.
External/policy errors include `credential_unavailable`, `unknown_capability`, `unknown_action`, `unknown_skill`, `specialization_conflict`, `override_exceeds_pool`, `grant_conflict`, `authority_revoked`, `meta_grant_exceeds_authority`, `grant_limit_exceeded`, `fork_policy_conflict`, `fork_policy_widen_refused`, `profile_readback_mismatch`, `config_revision_conflict`, and `transport_unverified`. The reference validator deliberately does not claim it can prove these external effects.

### 4. Cross-record semantics and operational meaning

### 4.1 Identity, membership and resources
* IDs are globally unique across agents and workers; gateway, room, project, peer and registry IDs are unique within their registries. `hermesBinding.instance == gateway`, and that gateway exists. Profile names are distinct `(instance,profile)` pairs matching `pf-…`; `default` is forbidden. `identity.principal_id` is globally unique. Protected session/learned-state references cannot be shared. Gateway `host_id` names the enrolled host and must match profile readback; two gateways may address one host only if their instance/profile bindings remain distinct. * `identity.policy_owner == vp.owner`. It is never inferred from the sender, room, parent bond or transport. Profile credentials are looked up from `identity.credential_ref`; the gateway token authenticates controller transport and cannot substitute for another profile's credential. * Each agent/worker has exactly one matching registry row; responsibility equals the actor's responsibility string; mirror key equals `/chd/registry/<id>`. Unknown extra rows fail. Registry mirroring is controller-owned; it conveys responsibility, not capability. * All room participants exist. Room kind matches its ID prefix. For actors with a `rooms` array, membership is bidirectional between that array and `participants`. Worker assignment room membership is established by the authorized assignment operation, not guessed from a worker ID. `agents[].session.objective` is a bootstrap room reference despite its historical name; the actor is a participant. An objective/task bond matches room kind; `self` is a self session associated with the explicit room. `session_key` is a configured logical seed, never a promise that a particular native session already exists; branch/native session identities belong in runtime bond records. * `composition.project_scope` is an explicit list of instruction roots; `projects[].workdirs` maps named project IDs for policy overrides. Multiple selected projects are explicit request context. Do not choose one by lexicographic path or first match. Actual dispatch paths are checked against `allowed_workdirs` after target-side realpath resolution. * Tool include/exclude entries are exact registered tool identifiers in this candidate, not wildcard toolsets. Lists cannot overlap; every included tool has an explicit use capability. An excluded tool cannot run even when a use grant exists. The production loader resolves tool/capability IDs against the adapter's authoritative catalog, not a hardcoded fixture list. Skills do not grant tools. Unknown strings must fail, not silently disappear.

### 4.2 Caps, clocks, waits and no-op
All admission dimensions are independent and conjunctive: gateway `max_inflight`; the additional global gateway ceiling `dispatch.max_inflight_per_gateway`; actor `max_sessions`; `capacity.per_role.<role>` across the namespace; actor/worker `max_parallel`; and `orchestration.max_fanout` per send composition. The effective gateway run ceiling is the minimum of its row and dispatch ceiling. Actor room-kind concurrency and native live-session counts are different units; worker `max_parallel` is its concurrent managed-run count. Values are not multiplied or inferred from one another. Zero room-kind/per-role cap disables new running work in that class, **not** enqueueing or scheduling. Capacity reduction does not kill in-flight work; new reservations wait until usage falls below all limits.
`dispatch.admission_authority: controller` fixes the owner of the shared reservation ledger for **all** paths. `admission.run_now_owner: controller_local` permits immediate admission without a scheduler round trip. `scheduler` means an additional required scheduler approval gate, never a second reservation ledger. In controller-local mode `scheduler_bump_fallback: true` permits a queued immediate request to request a normal scheduler wake using the same identity; it does not bypass backpressure or create a second run. Set false in scheduler-owner mode because the scheduler is already primary. Scheduler-down cold start may be read/immediate-ready with verified storage and gateways in controller-local mode, but must report scheduled-not-ready; scheduler-owner mode cannot dispatch new work until its approval path is ready. These select explicit deployment behavior rather than globally assuming outage means ready or unready.
`scheduler.callback_url` is exactly `<ingress.public_url>/v1/triggers/fire`. The ingress credential reference authenticates the owner surface; callback credentials authenticate the scheduler as a restricted trigger principal, not unrestricted VP. Agent principals resolve from their profile credential binding. All API/MCP/CLI/webhook doors use that same authentication/authorization policy. Enabling a UI or bridge never grants posting authority. UI stays room-scoped/read-only unless the caller independently holds a named VP posting grant.
`worker.direct_gateway` must be false. `worker.timeout_s` requests cancellation and verified stop, never synthetic success. `progress_interval_s` bounds progress-write frequency. `capacity.unresolved_hold_s` is an escalation threshold, not auto-release TTL. Probe backoff is bounded at 900s; failures retain the reservation until positive runtime stop proof is committed. A report alone, elapsed lease, waiting status or process absence does not prove stop.
Verify deadlines/follow-ups detect silence and notify/escalate; they do not approve or resume human waits. `max_followups: 0` disables follow-ups. Follow-ups are scheduler triggers, with the source's per-gate dedupe/cap; no CHD scheduling engine. `stale_after_s` marks stale pending composition for reconciliation, never erases the logical obligation. Fresh-report validation uses trusted ingest timestamps and request/attempt correlation, not configurable permissiveness.
No hierarchy is a legal no-op: use empty `agents`, `workers`, `rooms`, `registry`, `dispatch.targets`; disable scheduler/bridge/federation and manager creation, with all required infrastructure/security fields explicit. It creates no hierarchy rooms/triggers/runs. Missing/empty file is invalid, not an implicit deployment. This is the exact reconciliation of DESIGN R-012 with strict required fields.

### 4.3 Storage, archive, federation and measurement
* `duckbrain.base_url` and `storage.controller.backend_url` identify the same control-store origin. Namespace is separate from a key path; e.g. namespace `chd`, key `/chd/registry/director`. No local SQLite durability substitute is authorized. * `coordination_report` and `control_key`: namespace equals root namespace; backend controller; immediate sync; no proxy; `controller_fsync` acknowledgement. Control/report writes never route to project memory. Controller storage outages leave work queued/blocked. * `session_archive`: distinct namespace equal to `archive.namespace`; controller backend; checkpointed sync; `committed_checkpoint`. Advertisement follows committed checkpoint readback. `archive.read_scopes` is the maximum grantable scope, not a read grant. Retention and checkpoint cadence are required explicit; retained restore manifests/checkpoints must remain verifiable under the archive contract. No raw native payload format is invented here. * Project memory disabled: backend none, namespace/sync_owner/conflict_rule null, sync disabled, proxy none, acknowledgement none. Enabled: isolated nonempty namespace, background sync, explicit sync_owner/conflict_rule, acknowledgement `local_enqueue_not_complete`; local/federated routes require controller proxy. `conflict_rule` is a named registered rule (`controller_wins`, `local_wins_on_project_keys`, or `checkpoint_order` where applicable), not executable text. Enabled sync must have exactly one writer per namespace. Disabled fields do not imply authority. * Every class's `readback_field` equals `<class>.backend`. `storage.tool_class` maps exact registered operation names. All enabled persisted operations must be mapped; unknown/unmapped operations fail closed. The full example maps only its enabled tool surface; extending that surface requires explicit mappings. * Federation requires authenticated peer identity and a live unexpired onboarding record; allowed_scopes are maximum local bounds. `local_vp_precedence` and `no_sender_vp` must both be true. No peer ID or successful mTLS handshake confers local VP. Expiry is UTC RFC3339 `Z`, no inferred expiry. Disabled federation performs no peer dispatch. * `measurement.window_cycles` compares adjacent windows, `nonregression_tolerance_pct` is a percentage (divide by 100 when applying), and the two-element token band is ordered low ≤ high. They configure reporting only and cannot certify an unexecuted soak. Example values are not measured performance results.

### 5. Precedence: VP > director > manager
There are **not three config files** to merge. The VP owns this entire desired document. Director/manager changes are authorized, provenance-bearing control-store records, not arbitrary YAML patches. For each exact `(recipient, capability, resource, authority-class)` decision:
1. Authenticate issuer and verify current grant lineage, expiry/revocation, resource/recipient subset, delegation depth, count, conferable bounds and approval. Reject invalid records before resolution. A role name by itself grants nothing. 2. Apply VP explicit policy first, then valid director delegation, then valid manager delegation. **Explicit deny wins over lower-layer allow; absence is not a deny**, but grants still cannot exceed the VP's maximum authorized pool. A missing use grant is deny-by-absence unless a valid authorized delegation supplies it. A VP `room_read` scope `[]` is an explicit empty standing scope, never a wildcard. 3. Same-rank conflicting live proposals for the same tuple fail `grant_conflict`; do not choose arrival order. Revisions supersede their own prior record by explicit lineage, not by timestamp arbitration. 4. Specialization may refine base role only inside `authorized_overrides` and exact authorized grant deltas, below VP/director/manager constraints. Project instructions → base-role → specialization is instruction composition order, **not** permission authority order. Neither instruction text nor a skill can grant a right. 5. Record winning value/source and every rejected conflicting source in readback/audit. An out-of-bound proposal fails even if another higher-ranked value would mask it. Never briefly apply a losing value.
| VP bound / decision | Director decision | Manager decision | Result | |---|---|---|---| | bound allows; explicit deny | allow | allow | denied, VP origin; conflict audited | | bound allows; no explicit decision | explicit deny | allow | denied, director origin | | bound excludes tuple | none | allow | deny / reject outside-authority manager record | | bound allows; no explicit decision | none | valid delegated allow | allowed, manager origin | | bound allows; explicit allow | deny | deny | VP allow remains; attempted conflicting lower update audited | | no valid use grant from any source | none | none | deny-by-absence |
A manager may grant a capability it cannot itself use **only** if `permissions.grant` independently authorizes it. `confer_delegation` is separately required to issue another grantor. The example intentionally gives `mgr-infra` grant-use for `telegram.send` without Telegram use or tool inclusion. `use.recipients` is self only: roles/agents/pools empty and tiers `[self]`. Recipient selectors on delegation scopes are explicit permitted sets; empty lists permit no recipients except the explicit self use convention. A recipient must match a configured tier and, if roles/agents/pools constrain it, satisfy those bounds; multiple named agent/pool selectors union within that dimension, then intersect with tier/role/resource/VP bounds. Unknown pools or archive agents are errors. `max_depth:0` forbids conferring delegation; `max_grants:0` permits no outstanding downstream grants. Limits apply to new issuance, not as permission inheritance.

### 5.1 Create and approval rules
Tier order is director > manager > supervisor > foreman > worker. `create_subordinate:none` denies creation. Any other value is the highest tier a holder may create; only strictly lower tiers than the holder are eligible, within the named ceiling. A supervisor has no grant/confer authority; a configured creation permission does not turn it into a policy chooser. Worker cannot create anything. Creation requests require explicit authorized templates, capacity, gateway pool, unique profile, token provisioning and readback. Director-created managers additionally require `hierarchy.manager_creation.enabled:true` and positive remaining `max_director_created`. Disabled returns `manager_creation_disabled`. Provisioning is pending until operator token setup/readiness, never automatically armed.
`approvals.human_approval_required:true` gates every mutating operation for that actor; otherwise `gates` names the exact mutating action classes requiring recorded human approval. An empty gates list with false means no extra profile-wide gate, **not** a permission grant. Assignment-specific human gates and delegation `limits.require_approval` are conjunctive extra gates: no lower layer can remove them. Gate names resolve against the authoritative action catalog during readiness. A timer is not approval.

### 5.2 Activation and evidence
| Field group | Writer | Activation | |---|---|---| | File, identities/bindings, skills, caps, membership, triggers, runtime, approvals, storage and specialization asset selection | VP/operator only | Atomic desired revision after full validation; external convergence/readback before target readiness | | Caps and room membership | VP/operator | Next orchestrator/router check; never retroactively kill current runs | | Trigger changes | VP/operator | Next verified scheduler-registration pass | | Skills/runtime/tool availability/composition | VP/operator | Next NEW session or REUSE turn; in-flight turn retains captured config digest | | Permission/approval policy | VP roots plus authorized bounded grant records | New session/fork/restore or explicit authorized resync; existing live snapshot not silently refreshed | | New grant issuance and archive page access | Authorized issuer/reader | Current lineage checked each issuance/page, including revocation; live-use snapshot is not issuance authority | | Fork-mode maps / resync enablement | VP/operator | Future fork/resync authorization boundaries only |
This explicitly resolves the VOLD-008 “next REUSE tools/approvals” wording against frozen policy: profile runtime/tool availability may change at a turn boundary, but policy rights/approval requirements in the live snapshot do not mutate automatically. A newly available tool still needs frozen use authority; a removed tool is unavailable even if a frozen grant remains. Effective-config and session-policy readbacks must expose that distinction.
`GET /v1/effective-config/{agent-id}` must return desired and profile-reported effective revisions/digests, drift/readiness, explicit identity and protected-state refs, and **each resolved leaf's value, winning authority (`vp|director|manager|specialization|base|default`), source reference and activation boundary**. Config-scope current policy is not session-scope frozen authority. `GET /v1/policy/effective?session=<bond-id>` must reproduce the stored snapshot and digest. `GET /v1/effective-routing` includes class, backend, namespace, sync, proxy, credential reference name (no secret), digest and project sync checkpoint/lag. Readback schemas/transport ownership remain the sibling operation-contract deliverable; this defines required content, not a fabricated endpoint response.
